description: How high a 3D map stands an airspace volume: its floor and top in feet MSL, from its limits as the FAA's data gives them (each its figure in feet, a flight level times 100, its CODE SFC, AGL, MSL, STD or UNLTD and its DESC TI, TNI or ANI), read as special_use_tab reads them: SFC above 0 is that height above the ground, a ceiling "to but not including" a foot under its figure (FL180 TNI 17,999 ft MSL), a floor "above but not including" a foot over it. A floor above the ground stands on the lowest of `ground`, a ceiling on its highest; the surface is 0 ft MSL with `surface` true; a flight level is drawn as if MSL; no ceiling, or one above it, is drawn to 18,000 ft MSL, where Class A begins (14 CFR 71.33(a)), a drawing bound. Null where nothing is left to draw, or where a limit above the ground has no `ground`.

ground.description: The ground under the volume, ft MSL: its lowest and its highest. Null where the map has none in yet.

surface.description: Whether the floor is the surface, drawn from the sea up.
